title: Bechet's trial and Bullard's plea to the judge
summary: Facing the guillotine, Bechet wailed in court until Bullard, in his medals, explained Bechet's superstitions to the judge, who freed both men upon payment of indemnities.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition

So the state attorney says these rascals are shooting up our civil population, shooting at great artists like Mr. McKenzie. I have no other alternative but to have the death sentence, the guillotine must (inaudible).
Bechet started to cry. And his hands reached up like he was looking for somebody, help from somebody, and hollered, "Mama, Mama, "No, no!" Then the judge says, "Silence, Silence!" Bechet

was (inaudible) "Please come and get me." The judge says, "Silence." Then the prosecuting attorney says, Mr. McKenzie, who's a gentleman, comes here to entertain us and this rousta-bout thug, everything! Almost indicated that he broke out from prison camp or something, or plantation in New Orleans. And Bechet he was from moaning, going on.

So, "I say again, let the guillotine do its duty for things of this nature." Bechet started crying and moaning back, and went into convulsions. and got on the floor and wallowed on his /The judge says, "Arrete! Arrete!" "Get him un from there!" So they got Bechet back in there, helped him (inaudible). And the judge was whispering -- see there are three judges, you know, sometimes four. And they began to whisper to this main judge. The main judge pointed at Bechet and Bechet went into his act again.

So Gene Brouillard was sitting in the court and the judge looked at Bechet and he's about to bow his head. I think I'd better do something to him. So he and Brouillard come up immediately. He says, "Judge," and he had all these medals on him, all from when he was in the Foreign Legion, Croix de Guerre, Legion de Honor (inaudible).

"May I have a word?" And the lawyer for Mike McKenzie, his name was Torez, a great lawyer, one of those type of lawyers at that time. So he said, from what bar are you? And Gene Brouillard says, "I'm from the bar of justice," fraternite, egalite." They have justices -- you know, in all courts you have the main judge (inaudible).

So he began his speech. "I've given my blood for France. I love France. That's why I'm here. That's why this man's here, that's why this Mr. McKenzie is here. Things haven't been so well for Mr. Bechet. See, he has lost his mother and that's why when you spoke of the guillotine, he could see people from where he comes are very, very superstitious. And he was feeling that his mother would come and get him or come and change your mind about that guillotine."

Bechet went through that stuff again. Judge says, all right, be careful. He reached over to Bechet, "Be quiet." Then he said, "So that is why." He says, "Oh, yeah?" He asks him from where he come. He says, he come from Louisiana State. Well, that's French. "What is your name?" "Sidney Bechet." (Inaudible).

So Torez, "A word, please." (Inaudible) the judge says -- Gene Brouillard looked at Torez says, "I'm going to knock you out if you don't be careful." The judge says, "What did you say?" "Oh, nothing, Judge."

So he had the judge, had the whole court stupefied. that was And the audience, //drama. So Bechet, he was (inaudible). So all these other judges were whispering in this judge's ear. And the judge, he looked at them kind of, what are you doing, trying to tell me what to do with this case. He looked at them and took the gavel, wham, wham, wham.
"I've watched this case. In this case I want each

to walk out of this court free. But you must pay indemnities to all these people you have harmed. All the way. We will give you the price. We will give you the sum you must pay. You may leave." But Bechet's still there crying. So the judge say, "You may leave the court, the court is closed." Then they all go into the chamber. Bechet says, "I can't leave with this suit on because I have no clothes." And one of the guards gets Bechet some coat or something to put on his back. And that's what happened to Gene Bullard.
Oh, you mean he had on one of those prison suits?
Yeah, Bechet was -- they'd drawn him out from under the river. That's bad news. His hair turned white. Turned white. That was Bechet.
